title: Minimal-touch ablation response to an uncooperative co-orbital approach
epochLabel: Configured epoch; representative orbits, not an element set

holdText.REASSESS: re-assessing predicted separation after a touch
holdText.GEOMETRY: beam not within 60° of the target velocity (prograde push)
holdText.BEAM_SAFETY: protected satellite within 0.10° of the beam axis
holdText.CLEARED: separation criteria met; no further touches

summary.scenario: COSMOS 2612 / ICEYE-X36 stand-in, representative 545 km sun-synchronous orbit

events.message: Unperturbed closest approach in 15.3 h at 54 m; floor 2 km, re-open to 6.25 km by that epoch
Touch 1: firing at 151 km from behind, asset 0.14° off the beam axis beyond the target
Touch 1 done: 1.24 cm/s prograde, 208 kJ on target; predicted minimum 2.04 km, 2.05 km at the original TCA
protected asset within 0.10° of the beam axis
Touch 2: firing at 166 km from behind, asset 0.10° off the beam axis beyond the target
Touch 2 done: 1.24 cm/s prograde, 208 kJ on target; predicted minimum 3.97 km, 3.97 km at the original TCA
Touch 3: firing at 149 km from behind, asset 0.16° off the beam axis beyond the target
Touch 3 done: 1.24 cm/s prograde, 208 kJ on target; predicted minimum 4.65 km, 5.89 km at the original TCA
Touch 4: firing at 133 km from behind, asset 0.14° off the beam axis beyond the target
Touch 4 done: 1.24 cm/s prograde, 208 kJ on target; predicted minimum 4.65 km, 7.81 km at the original TCA
Predicted minimum 4.65 km ≥ 2 km floor and 7.81 km at the original TCA ≥ 6.25 km; no further touches
threshold cleared; monitoring to closest approach

limits: Representative orbits from published figures (545 km, 97.8°, ~5 km station-keeping, tens-of-metres predicted miss); no element set, epoch or spacecraft design is represented.
Intruder treated as uncooperative and non-manoeuvring during the response; a cooperative or actively manoeuvring spacecraft can undo any nudge.
Ablation coupling 50 µN·s/J × 0.6 surface-normal efficiency at optimum fluence; energy on target follows spot-to-area ratio × 0.7 pointing efficiency. Assumptions, not measurements.

Surface effect is estimated from momentum coupling and a 10 km/s plasma velocity; it says nothing about which surface is hit. Optics, radiators and solar cells are damaged at far lower fluence than structure.
Beam safety is a single angular clearance rule for the protected asset; no model of pointing jitter distribution, other traffic, or ground illumination.
Gravity: point mass plus J2 at 1 s RK4; no drag, radiation pressure or attitude dynamics. Predictions are gravity-only propagation without tracking error; the margin factor stands in for covariance.
Closest-approach distances are geometric; no collision probability is computed.
